summary: A flat map of land dots with markers. Values light halos of dots sized by area, which spring to new values; labels place themselves.

props.name: markers
props.description: The places: `{ id, label?, lat, lon, value?, tone?, size?, pulse? }`. `tone` is `accent`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive` or `muted`; `size` is `sm`, `md` or `lg` (a 6, 8 or 10 px dot); `pulse` sends a ring of light through the land dots every 2.4 s. Halos spring to new values when it changes. An empty array shows the plain land with `emptyText`.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected marker id (controlled), or `null` for none. Use with `onValueChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The marker selected at first when uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called when the user selects a marker or clears the selection (Escape, a second press on the selected marker, a click on the map).

props.name: projection
props.description: Map projection. Equal Earth keeps areas true, so halos compare fairly at every latitude.

props.name: pitch
props.description: Dot spacing in px, clamped to 3 to 8.

props.name: latRange
props.description: Latitude crop as `[south, north]` in degrees. Markers outside it are skipped.

props.name: maxHalo
props.description: Halo radius in px for the largest value on a map 660 px wide. The radius scales with the map width, from 60% to 150%.

props.name: labels
props.description: Which label chips show: the largest values that have room, only the selected one, or none. Hovered and focused markers always show theirs. Without the prop, maps narrower than 480 px use `selected`.

props.name: reveal
props.description: When the land prints itself: the first time a third of the map is on screen, right after mount, or never (drawn at once).

props.name: revealFrom
props.description: Marker id or `{ lat, lon }` point the reveal grows from.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats values for the label chips and the markers' accessible names. The default gives `48.2K`.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Text shown when `markers` is an empty array.

keyboard.action: Moves focus into the map. One marker holds the tab stop: the last one focused, else the selected one, else the first.
Move focus to the nearest marker in that direction on the map.
Move focus to the first / last marker in `markers` order.
Select the focused marker, or clear the selection when it is already selected.

accessibility: The root has `role="group"`, `aria-roledescription="map"` and the `label` as its `aria-label`.
Each marker is a native `<button>` with `aria-pressed` and an `aria-label` of its label (or id) and formatted value, for example "London, 48.2K".
The markers share one roving tab stop, so the map is a single Tab stop however many markers it has.
A marker focused from the keyboard shows its label chip and a 2 px accent focus ring.
The canvases and the label chips are `aria-hidden`; the chips repeat what the buttons already say.
motion: With reduced motion the land is drawn at once, halos appear at their size without the growth front, pulsing markers show a still ring of brighter dots, a selection changes without the ring, pop and sparks, and chip values change without rolling.
notes: Halo area is proportional to the value: the radius is `maxHalo · √(value / largest value)`, scaled with the map width. Zero, negative and missing values have no halo.
Halos light land dots only, so a coastal marker lights the land around it. Some coastal cities fall on water cells of the 0.5° land mask and show a partial halo.
Where halos overlap, each dot takes the brighter halo; nothing stacks.
With `labels="all"`, the largest values get chips, at most one per 120 px of map width. A chip that would cover another marker stays hidden.
Changing `projection`, `grid`, `pitch` or `latRange` after the first reveal prints the new lattice again from the selected marker, or from `revealFrom`.
A click on the map outside the markers clears the selection.
The root fills its container's width and keeps the projection's aspect ratio, so the server markup reserves the height and already places the markers.
Marker ids must be unique; a repeated id keeps its first marker.
Pulsing markers keep the animation running while the map is on screen. Without them it stops once everything has settled.

data.note: Pass your places as `markers`. Without it the map shows 14 demo cities with invented request counts.
